questions.question: Why can a film be called a "text"?
options: Because shots, sound and editing communicate meaning that can be read and analysed
Because films are based on books
questions.explanation: Film language — camera work, sound, editing — communicates meaning, so watching a film analytically is a form of reading.

questions.question: Why is it useful to understand film language in everyday life?
options: You constantly encounter visual media that try to influence your emotions and views
It is only useful for becoming a film director
Films are the only media that matter
It helps you avoid watching films
questions.explanation: Films, ads, social media videos and news broadcasts all use visual techniques to manipulate emotions — film literacy helps you see how.

questions.question: Which elements are part of film language?
options: The length of the end credits
questions.explanation: Every shot, camera movement, piece of music and edit contributes to the meaning of a film.

questions.question: What skill does analysing visual media help you develop?
options: Recognising bias and perspective in what you watch
questions.explanation: Studying film language helps you recognise bias and perspective and understand how images manipulate emotions.

questions.question: In which school task is film analysis directly useful?
options: Writing film reviews and analyses for English exams
questions.explanation: Understanding film language lets you write more insightful film reviews and analyses, which are relevant exam tasks.
